paragraphs.title: Job Recognizes His Limits After Encountering God

easy.explanation: The passage begins, “Then Job answered the LORD.”
easy.q: To whom does Job answer at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: Job says, “I know that thou canst do every thing.”
easy.q: What does Job acknowledge about the LORD’s ability?

easy.explanation: Job says, “now mine eye seeth thee.”
easy.q: Whom does Job say he now sees?

answers: He spoke about things beyond his understanding
He refused to speak at all
medium.explanation: Job confesses that he uttered things he did not understand, things too wonderful for him.
medium.q: Why does Job repent of his words?

answers: Nothing can prevent the LORD from carrying out His purposes
medium.explanation: Job declares that no purpose or plan can be withheld from the LORD.
medium.q: What does “no thought can be withholden from thee” mean?

answers: He moved from hearing about the LORD to seeing Him
He moved from speaking with friends to complete silence
He moved from wealth to poverty
medium.explanation: He says, “I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.”
medium.q: What change does Job describe between hearing about the LORD and his present experience?

answers: The direct encounter changed his understanding
He stopped believing in the LORD
He saw his friends instead of the LORD
challenge.explanation: The encounter led Job to recognize his limited understanding and respond humbly.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Job’s movement from hearing to seeing?

answers: Humility and recognition of human limitations
challenge.explanation: Job admits his lack of understanding and repents in dust and ashes.
challenge.q: What does Job’s response after the LORD’s words express?

answers: Speaking about things too wonderful for him to understand
challenge.explanation: He repents because he spoke of things he did not understand.
challenge.q: What does Job especially repent of?

paragraphs.title: God Vindicates Job and Commands His Friends to Make Amends

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends.”
easy.q: Against whom was the LORD’s wrath kindled?

easy.explanation: The LORD says the friends did not speak rightly, “as my servant Job hath.”
easy.q: Who spoke more rightly before the LORD?

easy.explanation: The LORD commanded them to take seven bullocks and seven rams.
easy.q: What were the friends commanded to take?

answers: Ask Job to pray for them
medium.explanation: The LORD said, “my servant Job shall pray for you.”
medium.q: What were the friends required to do with Job’s help?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes the LORD’s anger against the friends.
medium.q: What does the phrase “My wrath is kindled” mean?

answers: So that the LORD would not deal with them according to their folly
So that Job would give them an inheritance
So that they could receive Job’s possessions
medium.explanation: The LORD said that Job’s prayer would keep Him from dealing with them according to their folly.
medium.q: Why did the friends need Job’s prayer?

answers: The LORD vindicated Job and recognized his spiritual standing
The friends were stronger than Job
challenge.explanation: The friends had to seek the prayer of the man whom the LORD said had spoken rightly.
challenge.q: What does the command to go to Job suggest about Job’s position?

answers: Both were parts of the friends’ process of repentance
The offering was meant to make Job rich
The prayer was meant to replace the offering
challenge.explanation: The LORD commanded the friends to offer a burnt offering and have Job pray for them.
challenge.q: What relationship exists between the offering and Job’s prayer?

challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that they went and did what the LORD commanded.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the friends doing “according as the LORD commanded them”?

paragraphs.title: Job’s Prayer Leads to the Restoration of His Blessing

easy.explanation: The LORD turned Job’s captivity “when he prayed for his friends.”

answers: He turned the captivity of Job
He sent Job to his friends
easy.explanation: The verse says, “the LORD turned the captivity of Job.”
easy.q: What did the LORD do after Job prayed?

answers: His brethren, sisters, and former acquaintances
easy.explanation: All his brethren, sisters, and former acquaintances came to him.

answers: They ate with him, comforted him, and gave him gifts
They asked him to offer a sacrifice
medium.explanation: They ate bread with him, comforted him, and gave him money and gold.
medium.q: What did Job’s family and acquaintances do in his house?

answers: The LORD restored Job’s condition and fortunes
The LORD sent Job into exile
medium.explanation: The expression describes the restoration of Job’s circumstances.
medium.q: What does “the LORD turned the captivity of Job” mean in this context?

answers: The LORD restored Job after he prayed for his friends
Job lost his family before he prayed
His prayer caused the friends to leave
medium.explanation: The verse directly connects Job’s prayer for his friends with the LORD turning his captivity.
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between Job’s prayer and his restoration?

answers: He did not hold a grudge against them
challenge.explanation: Praying for them shows that Job was willing to help them despite their earlier words.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Job praying for his friends?

answers: Through shared food, comfort, and gifts
challenge.explanation: His relatives and acquaintances ate with him, comforted him, and gave him gifts.
challenge.q: How is the community’s return to Job described?

answers: His prayer is connected with the beginning of his restoration
His family returned before any change occurred
The gifts caused him to pray
challenge.explanation: The passage first describes Job’s prayer and restoration, then the arrival of his family and acquaintances.
challenge.q: What is the significance of the order between Job’s prayer and the return of his family?

paragraphs.title: Abundance, Family, and the Distinction of Job’s Daughters

easy.explanation: The passage says, “He had also seven sons and three daughters.”
easy.q: How many sons and daughters did Job have?

answers: No women in the land were as fair as they were
easy.explanation: The passage says that no women in all the land were as fair as Job’s daughters.
easy.q: How is the beauty of Job’s daughters described?

easy.explanation: Their father gave them “inheritance among their brethren.”
easy.q: What did Job give his daughters?

answers: He moved in with his friends
medium.explanation: The large numbers of animals show that Job was greatly blessed.
medium.q: What do the many sheep, camels, oxen, and asses show about Job’s condition?

answers: The later period of Job’s life
The name of one of his daughters
medium.explanation: It refers to Job’s circumstances later in life, when the LORD blessed him.
medium.q: What does “the latter end of Job” refer to?

answers: They received an inheritance among their brothers
medium.explanation: The passage specifically says that Job gave them an inheritance among their brethren.
medium.q: What was distinctive about Job’s daughters’ status?

answers: Their names and exceptional beauty are given
They were more numerous than his sons
challenge.explanation: The passage names the daughters and says that no women were as fair as they were.
challenge.q: What detail distinguishes the description of Job’s daughters from that of his sons?

answers: They were included in the family inheritance
They were not part of the family
challenge.explanation: An inheritance among their brothers indicates a recognized share in the family estate.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from giving the daughters an inheritance among their brethren?

answers: Through wealth, children, and a special inheritance for his daughters
Through the return of his friends alone
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions abundant possessions, seven sons, three daughters, and an inheritance for the daughters.
challenge.q: How is the LORD’s blessing of Job presented in this section?

paragraphs.title: Job’s Long Life and Peaceful End

easy.explanation: The passage says, “After this lived Job an hundred and forty years.”
easy.q: How many years did Job live after these events?

easy.explanation: Job saw his sons and his sons’ sons, “even four generations.”
easy.q: How many generations of descendants did Job see?

answers: On the way to his friends
easy.explanation: The final verse says that Job died “being old and full of days.”

answers: He enjoyed long life and an enduring family line
medium.explanation: Job lived many years and saw several generations of descendants.
medium.q: What does seeing four generations reveal about Job’s life?

answers: Satisfied after a full and complete life
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a person who has lived a full and satisfying life.
medium.q: What does the phrase “full of days” mean?

answers: He lived many years, saw generations, and died in old age
He died before his children were born
He left his family and returned to his friends
medium.explanation: The passage gives his years, the generations he saw, and then his death.
medium.q: What sequence is described at the end of Job’s life?

challenge.explanation: Job receives long life, sees descendants, and dies old and full of days.
challenge.q: What characterizes the ending of the book of Job?

answers: The blessing includes wealth, family, descendants, and long life
The blessing consists only of gifts
challenge.explanation: The closing verses extend the blessing beyond possessions to family and longevity.
challenge.q: How does Job’s ending relate to the blessing described in this chapter?

answers: Job lived another one hundred and forty years after the earlier events
Job lived only seven more years
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly states that Job lived another one hundred and forty years.
challenge.q: What is the central chronological detail in these verses?
